title: Sensory material architectures: Concepts and methodologies for spatial tectonics and tactile responsivity in knitted textile hybrid structures
research_question: How can textile-based hybrid structures be designed and fabricated using CNC knitting to create multi-scalar, sensory-responsive architectures that address challenges for children with autism spectrum disorder in filtering multiple sensory inputs?

participants.description: A single 5-year-old girl with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and sensory challenges, specifically under-responsivity to sensory stimuli, producing challenges in fine and gross motor control, verbal communication, behavioral regulation, and social interaction. Non-verbal.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but described as 'a single child is studied' in collaboration with therapists from occupational therapy (OT), applied behavioral analysis (ABA), and the Play and Language for Autistic Youngsters (PLAY) Project.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: StretchPLAY prototype: a multi-tubular seamless knitted textile hybrid structure with a bending-active Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) boundary, integrated with pressure-sensitive trigger points, a Microsoft Kinect for depth sensing, a projector for visual animations, and a sound system for auditory feedback.

Semi-toroidal Textile Hybrid prototype: a seamless textile cylinder with a four-sided textile panel, formed of highly elastic poly-elastan yarn with varied stitch structures (cast-off and all-needle) to achieve differential form-active stresses, integrated with a single bending-active boundary.

Mobius Rib-knit Textile Hybrid prototype: a rib-knit textile structure made of air-jet textured polyester yarn, with varying dimensions and number of ribs, designed to exploit the textile's natural recoiling behavior and produce an undulating tactile surface, integrated with a bending-active GFRP boundary.

measures.construct: Structural Displacement (under self-weight and point load)

measures.instrument: Microsoft Kinect for depth sensing, Unity gaming engine for processing, MadMapper for projection, sound system for audio playback
Close examination of movement, gestures, facial expressions; input from occupational therapists (OT), applied behavioral analysis (ABA), and PLAY Project therapists.

findings.consequent: Structural robustness and ability to resist significant point loads with minimal deflection
findings.mechanism: The lamination creates a bond between the rods and removes the possibility for shear movement, allowing for a more robust beam condition.
findings.quote: To develop a more robust beam condition, the knitted sleeve is impregnated in-situ with epoxy resin and vacuum-formed, creating a bond between the rods and removing the possibility for shear (Figure 11). Additionally, secondary GFRP rods are inserted to stabilize pivot points within the rod topology. Using fixed mechanical connections can cause peak stresses and failure at the interface between the rod and the connector. In this case, by using a consistent material type, the structure realizes a more fluid elasticity. With this multi-hierarchical system of GFRP rods and laminated GFRP beams, finite element analysis shows the ability to resist a significant point load with minimal deflection (Table 1 and Figure 12).

findings.antecedent: StretchPLAY prototype's interactive system (pressure-sensitive trigger points, visual animations, auditory feedback)
findings.consequent: Sensory regulating environment for children with SPD/ASD
findings.mechanism: The system provides acutely tailored relationships between scale, material elasticity, structural deformation, and visual, physical, and auditory feedback to counteract sensory overload.
findings.quote: To counteract this “traffic jam” of sensory data, the prototype promotes a sensory regulating environment by acutely tailoring the relationship between scale, material elasticity, structural deformation, and visual, physical, and auditory feedback.

findings.antecedent: StretchPLAY prototype's interactive system (trigger points requiring exploration and pressure)
findings.consequent: Gross motor movement and registration of touch
findings.mechanism: The effort of finding trigger points ensures exploration and gross motor movement. Strong resistance from the tensioned textile applies pressure to joints, aiding tactility and providing a calming effect for individuals with sensory processing difficulties.
findings.quote: The effort of finding trigger points ensures both an aspect of exploration, but also guarantees gross motor movement as a part of the playing process. The quality of resistance in pushing on the tensioned textile is an important feature in registering the sense of touch. With difficulties in sensory processing, a strong resistance applies pressure to the joints not just the hand and finger tips, giving a better chance for the tactility to be identified as well as providing a calming effect.

findings.antecedent: StretchPLAY prototype's interactive system (paired trigger activation for animations)
findings.mechanism: Once single-trigger activation becomes familiar, the system can unfold a social component by requiring two individuals to activate paired triggers, encouraging cooperation.
findings.quote: Certain animations play only when two triggers are simultaneously activated. Once the logic of finding and activating a single trigger to produce the visual and auditory feedback becomes familiar, the social component can be unfolded encouraging cooperation of two individuals to activate the paired triggers.

mechanisms: The architecture's responsiveness (visual, physical, auditory) enhances user comprehension of multi-sensory experience in time and space.
Tailoring deformability from hand to body scale coordinates movement and creates a coherent sensory spatial state.
CNC knitting allows for heterogeneous textile structures, manipulating fiber and knit structure to achieve simultaneous structural, spatial, and sensory-responsive qualities.
Rib-knit structures provide elasticity without elastic yarns, allowing for tailored textile behavior through varying rib dimensions and numbers.
Bundling and laminating small cross-section GFRP tubes creates robust bending-active beams with varied radii, resisting significant point loads with minimal deflection.
The interactive system (trigger points, visual/auditory feedback) provides filtered responsivity to sort and regulate multi-sensory input, addressing hyporesponsivity in SPD/ASD.
Strong resistance from the tensioned textile applies deep pressure to joints, promoting tactility and a calming effect.
The system's design encourages exploration, gross motor movement, and social cooperation through paired trigger activation.
implementation_implications: Architectures can serve as interfaces for human-computer interaction, embedding intelligence in responsiveness to enhance user comprehension of multi-sensory experience.
CNC knitting enables the explicit production of graded materials tailored for specific performative values, moving beyond standardized materials.
Textile hybrid systems can be designed to provide sensory regulating environments for individuals with Sensory Processing Disorder (SPD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).
The integration of pressure-sensitive textiles with visual and auditory feedback can create dynamically responsive playscapes that foster self-regulation, social engagement, and communication.
Designing for deep pressure and proprioceptive input through resistive textile surfaces can aid in sensory integration therapy, promoting tactility and calming effects.
Interactive architectural systems can be designed to encourage cooperative play and social interaction by requiring multiple users to activate features simultaneously.
The concept of 'calm technology' can guide the design of architectural systems that allow the periphery to shift attention without distraction, fostering focused states.

tables.description: Finite element analysis calculating self-weight and 40-lb point load on structure with only a single 0.5-inch diameter Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) rod (left) and a laminated GFRP beam with knitted sleeve (right). Bold values highlight maximum displacement.

limitations: The current research primarily focuses on the technological development of responsivity in textile structures.

Further research is needed to empirically measure the development of social skills and other human outcomes (e.g., self-regulation, social engagement, communication) through engagement with such architectures.
The study of human interaction is based on a single case (one child), limiting generalizability of behavioral observations.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: As the knowledge of material computation advances, continuing the seamless integration of design and fabrication, questions beyond materialization can be addressed with a focus on sensing, feedback, and engagement as critical factors of design exploration. This article will discuss a series of prototypes, design methodologies, and technologies that articulate a textile’s micro-architecture, at the scale of fibers and stitches, to instrumentalize simultaneous structural, spatial, and sensory-responsive qualities. The progression of research displays an ever-deepening instrumentalization of fiber structure and its implications to form definition and responsivity, in creating form- and bending-active structures. The research results in a more refined definition of material behavior as the innate phenomena which emerge at the moment of textile fabrication. Ultimately, the architecture, in its materiality and physical, visual, and auditory responsivity, is designed to address specific challenges for children in filtering multiple sensory inputs, an underlying factor of autism spectrum disorder.
